e.etymology: A spelling of Kaylyn, a modern American combination of Kay or Kayla with the -lyn ending.
A respelling of Alivia, itself a form of Olivia. Shakespeare used Olivia in Twelfth Night, and the name is generally tied to Latin oliva, olive.
From Tahitian maeva, welcome. It became fashionable in France in the late 20th century; in the US it is also heard as a longer form of Maeve.
The English name of the water flower, from Greek lotos by way of Latin. In Hinduism and Buddhism the lotus stands for purity, because it rises clean from muddy water.

assoc.t: lotus position, the cross-legged yoga pose

e.etymology: The Arabic form of Elijah, reaching Arabic from Hebrew Eliyahu, my God is Yahweh, by way of Greek Elias. Ilyas is named as a prophet in the Quran.
A modern American elaboration of Ava with the -aya ending of Amaya and Anaya.

assoc.t: Avaya, business phone and communications company

e.etymology: From Hebrew Mikhayahu, who is like Yahweh?, a close relative of Michael and the longer form of Micah. In 1 Kings the prophet Micaiah tells King Ahab the truth when 400 court prophets will not.
A spelling of Marley, an English surname from several place names that join Old English leah, woodland clearing, to a word for pleasant, boundary or marten.
From Sanskrit veda, knowledge. The Vedas are the oldest scriptures of Hinduism, so the name carries the sense of sacred learning.
A respelling of Emory, an English surname from the Norman name Emery, a form of Germanic Emmerich, whose second element means ruler. The spelling matches Emori, a character on the CW series The 100.

assoc.t: Emori, survivor on the CW series The 100

e.etymology: A spelling of Araceli, shortened from Maria de Araceli, a title of the Virgin Mary as patron of Lucena in Andalusia. It comes from Latin ara coeli, altar of heaven.
From Hebrew Tsefanyah, the Lord has hidden or sheltered. Zephaniah is one of the twelve minor prophets, with a short Old Testament book in his name.
A spelling of Ayaan, a name popular with both Muslim and Hindu families in South Asia and in their communities abroad.
A blend of Emma and Marie written as one name.

e.meaning: descendant of Aodhagán, little fiery one
e.etymology: A spelling of Keegan, an Irish surname from Mac Aodhagáin, son of Aodhagán. Aodhagán is a pet form of Aodh, an old Irish name meaning fire.
A respelling of Carson, a Scottish surname of uncertain origin that became an American first name, helped by the fame of frontiersman Kit Carson.
The Hebrew original of Elijah: El, God, plus -i, my, plus Yahu, a form of the divine name. Elijah was the prophet of the reign of King Ahab; Jewish tradition sets a cup for him at the Passover seder.
A Yiddish name, also spelled Bayla or Beila, traced either to a Slavic word for white or to Romance bella, beautiful. It is used mainly in Orthodox Jewish families.
e.note: In Spanish baila means he or she dances, or the command dance, so Spanish speakers will hear a verb.

e.etymology: A modern American name that joins the De- prefix to Amari or Mari, in the style of Demarcus and Jamari.
An Old Norse dwarf name from the Poetic Edda, usually read as bold or daring one and sometimes linked to Thor. J.R.R. Tolkien borrowed it for Thorin Oakenshield, the dwarf king of The Hobbit.
namesakes: Thorin Oakenshield (dwarf king in Tolkien's The Hobbit)

assoc.t: Thorin Oakenshield, dwarf king in The Hobbit

e.etymology: A pet form of Jane, the English feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. Janie was given as a full name most often around 1900.
namesakes: Janie Crawford (heroine of Their Eyes Were Watching God)

assoc.t: Janie's Got a Gun, 1989 Aerosmith hit

e.etymology: A modern coinage from Ava plus Lyn, or a variant of the medieval name Aveline.
From Latin pia, pious or dutiful, the feminine of the papal name Pius. It became a common given name in Scandinavia and Germany in the 20th century.
A modern American name built on the Hawaiian element lani, heaven or sky, in the style of Leilani and Kailani and close to the Hawaiian name Nalani.
The Greek form of the Phoenician name of Dido, the legendary founder and queen of Carthage. In modern use it also serves as a form of Elisa and Alyssa or a short form of Elizabeth.
A respelling of Keilani or Kailani, Hawaiian names built on lani, heaven or sky; Kailani adds kai, sea. The -y ending is common in Spanish-speaking American families.
A variant of the French name Germain, from Latin Germanus, which meant brother or kinsman and also German. Jermaine Jackson of The Jackson 5 made it popular in the 1970s.
The name of an Athenian woman converted by the apostle Paul in Acts 17. Its origin is uncertain; it may be a variation of Greek damalis, calf. Puritans revived it, and it is now common in Spanish.
The English word, from Old French riote, quarrel or dispute. It is a recent rebel-style name in the line of Rebel and Rogue; Rihanna and A$AP Rocky named their second son Riot Rose in 2023.

assoc.t: riot, the word for a violent public disturbance
Riot Games, maker of League of Legends

e.note: Riot is the everyday word for a violent public disturbance, and some people will find the name provocative.

e.etymology: The birth name of rapper XXXTentacion, Jahseh Onfroy, taken by his Jamaican father from the Bob Marley song So Jah Seh: Jah, the Rastafari name of God, plus seh, Jamaican Patois for says. Use rose after his death in 2018.

assoc.t: birth name of the late rapper XXXTentacion

e.etymology: A modern American name that joins Ryn, as in Kathryn or Camryn, to the -lee ending, alongside Rylee and Brynlee.
A respelling of Kaiser, the German word for emperor, which descends from the Roman title Caesar. It joins King, Prince and Kaiser among recent American title names.
e.note: Heard as Kaiser: the title of Germany's emperors, and the name of the Kaiser Permanente health system.
